name: Epitalon
lead: Epitalon, also spelled epithalon or epithalone, is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the amino acid sequence alanine-glutamic acid-aspartic acid-glycine (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly, AEDG) and the molecular formula C14H22N4O9.[1] It was designed from the amino acid composition of epithalamin, an extract of bovine pineal gland, and has been described as the putative active component of that preparation.[1][2] Most of the research on epitalon and epithalamin comes from the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology, led by Vladimir Khavinson, although laboratories elsewhere have recently begun to study it.[1]

It is promoted in anti-ageing circles for claims that it activates telomerase and lengthens telomeres. Laboratory work reports that it increases telomere length in human cell lines through telomerase upregulation or an alternative lengthening mechanism,[3] and Russian clinical reports claim effects on ageing markers.[1][4] Independent, large, placebo-controlled human trials are lacking, and a 2026 narrative review evaluates mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence for the synthetic peptide separately from the older extract.[4]

Epitalon is not approved as a drug by major regulators and is sold as a research chemical. On forums such as T Nation, it appears in peptide stacks discussed by members using unregulated products, an area in which product quality and dosing are not independently verified.
infobox: Not approved as a drug by major regulators; sold as a research chemical

paras: Epitalon is a short linear peptide made of alanine, glutamic acid, aspartic acid and glycine.[1][5] Grokipedia states it is produced by solid-phase peptide synthesis, that a Russian patent issued in 2001 described synthesis of such tissue-specific peptides, and that its short length makes it prone to degradation in solution, so it is typically lyophilised for storage.[5] Epithalamin, the extract it was derived from, is a chemically distinct pineal-derived polypeptide preparation.[4]

Epithalamin was isolated from bovine pineal glands in the 1970s by Khavinson and V. N. Anisimov, according to Grokipedia, which also describes the work as growing from Soviet-era military gerontology programmes at the Kirov Military Medical Academy in Leningrad.[5] Khavinson later founded the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology in 1992, and the AEDG tetrapeptide was identified from epithalamin's amino acid analysis and synthesised in the early 1990s.[5] A 2002 review described a technology for manufacturing complex peptide preparations from tissue extracts, with the pineal preparation epithalamin augmenting growth of pineal explants in vitro.[2] Early papers from the group reported an increase in the lifespan of Drosophila exposed to epitalon during development.[6]

The compound's profile outside Russia grew in the 2000s and 2010s through anti-ageing literature and peptide vendors, and recent years have seen studies from other laboratories, including work on telomere length in human cell lines in 2025.[1][3]

Wikipedia reports that epitalon appeared to induce telomere elongation through increased telomerase activity in human fibroblast cultures, extending their proliferative capacity beyond the Hayflick limit in one experiment, and that it decondensed heterochromatin in lymphocytes from elderly donors and reduced production of the protein MMP9 in ageing skin fibroblasts.[1] A 2025 Biogerontology study reported that epitalon increases telomere length in human cell lines through telomerase upregulation or ALT activity.[3] Group reports also describe epigenetic effects on gene expression and protein synthesis during neurogenesis,[7] antioxidant properties of pineal peptides,[8] restoration of pineal and pancreatic hormonal functions,[9] and effects on proliferative activity and inflammatory pathways in a monocyte cell line.[10]

Whether these effects occur at meaningful levels in living humans after injection or nasal use has not been established by independent studies. Grokipedia notes that epitalon is proposed to influence melatonin synthesis and that animal results on lifespan have been mixed.[5]

In animals, researchers report lifespan extension in fruit flies,[6] reduced spontaneous mammary tumours in HER-2/neu transgenic mice,[11] inhibition of colon carcinogenesis induced by dimethylhydrazine in rats,[12] and restoration of disturbed neuroendocrine regulation in senescent monkeys.[13] A study of stressors and antistressors on lifespan in HER-2/neu mice is also cited.[14] Wikipedia additionally cites reduced chromosomal aberrations in ageing mice, increased antioxidant enzymes in rats and reduced tumour counts in C3H/He mice.[1] Epitalon preserved retinal function in a rat model of retinitis pigmentosa,[15] protected mouse oocytes from post-ovulatory ageing in vitro,[16] enhanced delayed wound healing in an in vitro model of diabetic retinopathy,[17] and improved maturation and embryo development in bovine oocytes.[18] These findings come from cell and animal systems.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists an early phase 1 study of systemic and topical geroprotective rejuvenation assessed with ageing clocks (n=48), enrolling by invitation with a start date in October 2026.[19]

The human literature on epitalon is small and comes mainly from Russian groups. Wikipedia summarises reports that epitalon and epithalamin each increased telomere length in blood cells of patients aged 60 to 65 and 75 to 80 with comparable efficacy, that they appeared to restore melatonin secretion in aged monkeys and humans, that a trial in retinitis pigmentosa found a positive clinical effect in 90 percent of treated patients, and that in tuberculosis patients epitalon did not correct existing chromosomal aberrations but appeared to protect against new ones.[1][15] The retinitis pigmentosa paper is a controlled clinical trial that also reports effects in a rat model.[15]

Wikipedia also cites prospective cohort studies of epithalamin, the extract, and not synthetic epitalon: a cohort of 266 people over age 60 in which treatment was associated with a 1.6 to 1.8 fold reduction in mortality over six years, with larger reductions when combined with thymalin, and a cohort of 79 coronary patients over more than 12 years with lower cardiovascular and overall mortality.[1] Grokipedia describes limited human studies mainly from the same group and states that broader clinical validation, including independent phase 1 safety studies, remains necessary.[5] A 2025 review and a 2026 narrative review assess the mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence,[4][20] and a 2026 gerontology review places epitalon among peptide therapeutics for healthy ageing.[21] No independent randomised placebo-controlled trial of epitalon for ageing or appearance outcomes was found.

Grokipedia reports no severe adverse events in long-term Russian trials of related preparations and low toxicity in preclinical data, while emphasising that independent clinical validation is lacking.[5] Because telomerase activity is also a feature of many cancers, researchers and commentators discuss theoretical concerns about telomerase-activating compounds, although animal studies from the originating group report reduced rather than increased tumour incidence.[11][12][1] Epitalon is sold as an unregulated research chemical, so product identity, purity and sterility are not covered by regulatory oversight.

Epitalon is sold by peptide vendors for research use and discussed in anti-ageing communities as a telomere peptide and pineal bioregulator. On T Nation, one 2017 thread on peptides alongside testosterone replacement describes epitalon as improving neuronal firing in the prefrontal cortex,[22] and a 2023 poster asks whether to run it in a separate phase after a stack of other peptides.[23] These are user reports and not controlled data. No looksmax.org or Reddit material was identified in this review.

timeline.event: Epithalamin, a bovine pineal extract, is isolated by Khavinson and Anisimov, per Grokipedia.[5]
Khavinson founds the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology.[5]
The tetrapeptide AEDG (epitalon) is identified and synthesised from epithalamin's amino acid composition.[5]
A study reports that epitalon increased lifespan of Drosophila melanogaster.[6]
Reports of effects in a retinitis pigmentosa model and in tumour-prone mice are published.[15][11]
A Biogerontology study reports telomere lengthening in human cell lines.[3]
A narrative review evaluates mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence for epitalon.[4]

lore.intro: In anti-ageing and peptide communities epitalon is described as a telomere-lengthening pineal peptide; on T Nation it appears in short peptide-stack threads and is credited with cognitive and longevity benefits.[22][23]

claims.claim: Epitalon lengthens telomeres and slows ageing
claims.believers: Proponents cite Khavinson-group reports of telomerase activation and increased telomere length in cells and in blood cells of older patients.[1][3]
claims.experts: The cell-line result was reported in 2025, but reviews note that most data come from one research group and that independent human trials are lacking; a 2026 narrative review evaluates mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence separately.[3][4][5]

claims.believers: Supporters point to Russian cohort studies showing lower mortality in older people given the pineal extract.[1]
claims.experts: Those cohorts used epithalamin, the extract, rather than synthetic epitalon, and were not independent randomised trials; animal lifespan results are mixed according to Grokipedia.[1][5]

claims.claim: Epitalon improves cognition and brain function
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says it improves firing of prefrontal cortex neurones and wakes quiescent ones.[22]
claims.experts: Group publications report effects on gene expression during neurogenesis in cell systems; no controlled human cognition trial was found.[7]

claims.claim: Epitalon is anti-cancer, or alternatively could promote cancer via telomerase
claims.believers: Some supporters cite the mouse and rat studies showing fewer spontaneous mammary tumours and colon tumours.[11][12]
claims.experts: Those findings come from the originating group in animals; the theoretical concern about telomerase activation has not been tested in human trials of epitalon.[1][5]

claims.claim: Epitalon repairs sleep and melatonin rhythms
claims.believers: Supporters describe it as a pineal bioregulator that restores melatonin secretion.[1]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports restored melatonin secretion in aged monkeys and humans in group studies; independent replication was not found.[1][13]
